t: A thin Bluetooth brain for building your own wireless keyboard.
steps: Buy a nice!nano from an authorized keyboard shop such as Typeractive or Little Keyboards.
Buy a second board for a split keyboard.
Solder sockets onto your keyboard circuit board and seat the nice!nano in them.
Set up your ZMK keyboard settings on GitHub and let GitHub Actions build the firmware file.
Double-tap the reset button to make a drive called NICENANO appear.
Drag the .uf2 firmware file onto that drive.
Pair the keyboard over Bluetooth and test every key.
Add a 3.7 V rechargeable lithium battery last, soldered to the B+ and B- pads.
meta: Open Board. From $24.99. A few stores.
